palettes.title: Mac Paint
palettes.description: Sampled from a genuine Apple Macintosh CRT in 2021, it uses the light blue and faded black to carry 1bit art in the closest you can get to looking at an Apple Macintosh screen's colours without sitting in front of one. Take note that the colours are sampled from a daylight photograph of actual hardware then manually adjusted to best match the image, and is thus a representation of how the art displays as opposed to how it's recorded in software (which definitely would've been true black or white). Anyone has permission to use this palette for any purpose.

This is my first palette and it is a small 8 colour palette I've made for paper and ink / parchment style designs. To be used for things like old scrolls and maps and to give the feel of old fasioned ink on parchment drawings. 

I made it by taking various stock images of old scrolls and maps and condencing the colours down then tweaking them to work with my sprites.

Any comments or suggestions for improvment would be greatly appriciated.

images.title: Images
images.description: Image(s) to quantize (PNG base64). Several frames are quantized together onto ONE shared palette and must all be the same size — pass an animation's frames or a character's directions in one call so their colors stay consistent.

num_colors.title: Num Colors
num_colors.description: Target number of colors. Omit to auto-detect a good palette size from the image itself. Mutually exclusive with palette_image.

palette_image.description: An image whose colors become the palette (max 256 colors). Use it to force frames onto an existing game palette. Mutually exclusive with num_colors.

dithering.title: Dithering
dithering.description: Ordered dithering matrix size. Larger matrices give smoother gradients at the cost of a busier look.

dithering_strength.title: Dithering Strength
dithering_strength.description: How strongly to dither. Ignored when dithering is 'none'.
